reason: The logic is equivalent (.next = SEC then next_c's body inline; DEC/BIT leave C, BEQ done reaches 51 bytes on), but it grows bank 4 by 17 bytes (DEC ds_c 2, BEQ 2, BIT dm_flip 2, BPL 2, LDA 2, SBC 2, STA 2, BCC 2, JMP 3 = 19, less the BRA's 2), and bank 4 does not have the room in every build the project ships or proves with. The listings put DATA1's end (the SKIP PAD_END before REN_BASE &B400) at &B3F6 in the gameplay disc (build/strykers-gameplay.lst, 10 bytes free, the same in the hud_rupture gameplay set) and at &B3F9 in the DEBUG_FULLREDRAW oracle (build/strykers-debug_fullredraw.lst, 7 free). The shipping build has 131 free (&B37D), but in those builds 17 more bytes trip src/main.6502's ASSERT * <= REN_BASE ('bank 4 overruns the renderer's workspace'). The gameplay disc would not assemble, and neither would the passlock/worldrun oracle the gate compares against. The +17 also moves everything in bank 4 after to_each (compiled_part, sprite_columns, compiled_table, sprite_straight), which the candidate says changes branch page crossings, so the measured saving is not just the BRA's 3 cycles.
